coverage: Fifty-two unit identities; metre and minute intentionally share lowercase m through contextual.json. Two approved explicit aliases have their own catalog and locale files. Adjacent duration components add with or without spaces, in any order and with repeated units: 30m1h = 90min and 1h30m15m = 105min. An all-ambiguous sequence such as 1m30m or 1m 30m keeps the accepted duration-sum reading (31 minutes) and length-product reading (30 square metres); this does not introduce addition of adjacent lengths. In the duration parse, the complete sequence is one quantity under outer operators: 1h30m * 2 gives 180 minutes and -1h30m gives minus 90 minutes. The unfinished 1h30 leaves the live result blank until the last component has a unit. Appending a quantity of a different dimension requires an explicit operator: 1h30m2km is rejected with a brief missing-operator diagnostic, whereas 1h30m / 2km is an explicit pace calculation. The exact diagnostic wording is not yet selected. These rules preserve both accepted parses of 1m30m / 1m 30m and do not change ordinary precedence for its length-product parse or implicit multiplication generally. Identical-looking answers are grouped for display; supported compound-unit families are checked after final cancellation. Interpretations with unsupported final units are discarded when supported alternatives remain. Other branch errors are resolved by the round-23 extension described below. Contextual-units round 8 extends automatic superscript 2/3 formatting to every known length symbol and explicit length alias in the Latin baseline plus one active locale. Format only a complete unit shorthand: cm2 displays as cm² and metre3 as metre³, while m20 and m2rate retain their ordinary characters; continuing the word removes the superscript formatting. Backspace immediately after m² removes only the exponent, leaving m. Undo restores the previous user input without a separate automatic-formatting step. Clipboard representation, pasted-text behavior, persistence and other caret positions remain open. Round 23 accepts numerical branch-error filtering and correlated named-value meanings; calendar support is now requested in a separate decision, without redefining fixed-duration units.
